title: Personal Portfolio Website
description: Personal portfolio built with React, Vite and GitHub Actions - featuring dynamic project data from GitHub API, page routing, and a responsive carousel.
readme:
# Portfolio Website

Personal portfolio website built to showcase software engineering projects, skills, and experience.

---

## Evolution

| Version | Architecture |
|---------|-------------|
| `v1.0-html-baseline` | Static HTML |
| `v2.0-vanilla-js` | Vanilla JS, component-based, MVC pattern |
| `main` | React, Vite, SPA with routing |

---

## Current Architecture

Built with **React** and **Vite**, structured as a Single Page Application with client-side routing.

### Stack
- **Framework:** React 19 + Vite
- **Routing:** React Router DOM
- **Styling:** Custom CSS (carried over and extended from original)
- **Data:** GitHub Actions fetches project data from GitHub API daily and generates a static `projects.json`
- **Carousel:** Embla Carousel with autoplay
- **Markdown:** react-markdown + remark-gfm for project READMEs
- **Icons:** react-icons
- **Deployment:** GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages

### Pages
- `/` — Hero with introduction and call to action
- `/about` — Background and story
- `/experience` — Work experience
- `/education` — Academic background
- `/skills` — Technical and soft skills
- `/projects` — Auto-updating carousel of GitHub projects
- `/project/:slug` — Individual project page with rendered README
- `/contacts` — Contact links

### GitHub Action
A scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches all public repos via the GitHub API, extracts metadata (description, topics, language, README), and commits a static `projects.json` to the repo — keeping the portfolio always up to date without any manual intervention.

---

🔗 [katiavilarinho.dev](https://katiavilarinho.dev)

---

title: Study Clarify
description: Study & Clarify is an educational app that allows users to upload PDFs, read them, and get AI-powered explanations.
readme:
# Study-Clarify

An AI-powered study platform that turns PDF documents into interactive learning experiences. Upload an article, read it, explain its concepts to the AI, take an AI-generated quiz, and chat with an assistant that answers questions grounded in the document.

---

## Features

- **Topic & article management** — organise study material into topics; upload PDF files up to 10 MB
- **PDF viewer** — read documents directly in the browser
- **Progress system** — locked progression: read → explain → quiz
- **AI explanation** — write a free-text explanation of the document; the AI scores it (0–100) and gives feedback in your language
- **AI quiz** — generates 3 multiple-choice and 2 short-answer questions from the document; short answers are AI-evaluated
- **AI chat** — ask questions about the document; the AI only answers from its content
- **Dashboard** — overview of topics, articles, and completion rates
- **JWT authentication** — stateless, cookie-based; registration and login
- **Rate limiting** — per-endpoint protection via Bucket4j
- **Light / dark theme** — persisted across sessions

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend | Java 17, Spring Boot 4.0.2, Spring Security, Spring Data JPA |
| Database | PostgreSQL |
| Authentication | JWT (jjwt 0.11.5), HttpOnly cookies |
| PDF processing | Apache PDFBox 3.0.4 |
| Rate limiting | Bucket4j 8.5.0 |
| AI engine | Ollama (Mistral, local) |
| Frontend | React 19, Vite 7, Material UI 7 |
| Routing | React Router 7 |

---

## Prerequisites

- Java 17+
- Maven 3.9+
- Node.js 20.16+ or 22.3+
- PostgreSQL 14+
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com) running locally with the Mistral model pulled

```bash
ollama pull mistral
```

---

## Environment Variables

The backend reads the following variables at startup. Set them in your IDE run configuration, `.env` file, or shell before running.

| Variable | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `DB_URL` | JDBC connection URL | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/studyclarify` |
| `DB_USERNAME` | Database user | `postgres` |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | Database password | `secret` |
| `JWT_SECRET` | HS256 signing key (min 32 chars) | `my-super-secret-key-for-jwt-signing` |
| `JWT_EXPIRATION` | Token TTL in milliseconds | `86400000` (24 h) |
| `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | Ollama server URL | `http://localhost:11434` |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL_NAME` | Model name | `mistral` |
| `OLLAMA_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | Connection timeout (ms) | `10000` |
| `OLLAMA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | Read timeout (ms) | `120000` |
| `BASE_URL` | Public base URL of the application | `http://localhost:8081` |

---

## Running Locally

### 1. Database

Create a PostgreSQL database:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE studyclarify;
```

### 2. Backend

```bash
cd Backend/Study-Clarify
mvn spring-boot:run
```

The server starts on `http://localhost:8081/studyclarify`.

> The schema is created on startup (`ddl-auto=create`) and preserved on shutdown. Data persists across restarts.

### 3. Ollama

```bash
ollama serve          # if not already running as a service
```

Ollama listens on `http://localhost:11434` by default.

### 4. Frontend

```bash
cd Frontend/study-clarify-frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

The app is available at `http://localhost:5200`. The Vite dev server proxies `/studyclarify` to the backend automatically.

---

## Project Structure

```
Study-Clarify/
├── Backend/Study-Clarify/
│   └── src/main/java/dev/katiavilarinho/studyclarify/
│       ├── advice/          # Global exception handler
│       ├── controllers/     # REST endpoints
│       ├── converters/      # Entity → DTO converters
│       ├── dtos/            # Request / response records
│       ├── exceptions/      # Domain exceptions
│       ├── model/
│       │   ├── entity/      # JPA entities (User, Topic, Article, Progress, AI*)
│       │   └── enums/       # QuestionType, QuizStatus, Role
│       ├── persistence/     # Spring Data repositories
│       ├── rateLimit/       # Bucket4j configuration
│       ├── security/        # JWT filter, SecurityConfig
│       └── services/        # Business logic & Ollama integration
└── Frontend/study-clarify-frontend/
    └── src/
        ├── components/      # Reusable UI (NavBar, Folder, ArticleCard, AI panels)
        ├── context/         # AuthContext
        ├── hooks/           # useArticles, useProgress, useDashboard, …
        ├── layouts/         # AppLayout, AuthLayout
        ├── pages/           # Dashboard, Topics, TopicDetails, ArticleDetails, Login, Register
        ├── services/        # HTTP clients per domain (articles, quiz, explanation, …)
        ├── styles/          # Glass card styles, animations
        └── theme/           # MUI light and dark themes
```

---

## API Overview

All endpoints are prefixed with `/studyclarify/api`.

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/auth/register` | Create account |
| `POST` | `/auth/login` | Login and receive JWT cookie |
| `GET` | `/auth/me` | Current authenticated user |
| `GET` | `/topics` | List user topics |
| `POST` | `/topics` | Create topic |
| `PUT` | `/topics/{id}` | Update topic |
| `DELETE` | `/topics/{id}` | Delete topic |
| `GET` | `/topics/{topicId}/articles` | List articles in topic |
| `POST` | `/topics/{topicId}/articles` | Upload article (multipart/form-data) |
| `GET` | `/topics/{topicId}/articles/{id}/file` | Download PDF |
| `GET` | `/articles/{articleId}/progress` | Get reading progress |
| `POST` | `/articles/{articleId}/progress` | Initialise progress |
| `PATCH` | `/articles/{articleId}/progress/read` | Mark as read |
| `PATCH` | `/articles/{articleId}/progress/explanation` | Mark explanation submitted |
| `PATCH` | `/articles/{articleId}/progress/quiz` | Mark quiz completed |
| `POST` | `/articles/{articleId}/explanation` | Submit explanation for AI scoring |
| `GET` | `/articles/{articleId}/explanation/latest` | Get latest explanation result |
| `POST` | `/articles/{articleId}/quiz` | Generate quiz |
| `GET` | `/articles/{articleId}/quiz/{quizId}/questions` | Get quiz questions |
| `POST` | `/articles/{articleId}/quiz/{quizId}/submit` | Submit answers |
| `POST` | `/articles/{articleId}/conversations` | Start AI chat session |
| `POST` | `/articles/{articleId}/conversations/{id}/messages` | Send chat message |
| `GET` | `/dashboard` | Aggregated progress statistics |

---

## AI Progression

Each article follows a locked three-stage flow:

```
📄 Read  →  ✍️ Explain  →  🧠 Quiz
```

- **Read** — mark the article as read to unlock the explanation stage
- **Explain** — submit a free-text explanation; requires score ≥ 70/100 to unlock the quiz
- **Quiz** — 5 AI-generated questions; requires overall score ≥ 70 % to complete the article

---

## License

This project is for educational purposes.

title: Library Book Tracker (CLI)
description: CLI app to manage library books, clients, and loans — built with C# and a Strategy pattern for commands, with JSON file persistence.
readme:
# Library Book Tracker

A CLI application to manage a library's books, clients, and loans.

## Features

- Add, list, and remove books
- Add, list, and remove clients
- Loan and return books
- View loan history per client

## Architecture

```

├── CLI                 → Strategy pattern contract
│   ├── Commands
│   │   ├── Books       
│   │   │   ├── AddBookCommand.cs
│   │   │   ├── ListBooksCommand.cs
│   │   │   └── RemoveBookCommand.cs
│   │   ├── Clients
│   │   │   ├── AddClientCommand.cs
│   │   │   ├── ListClientsCommand.cs
│   │   │   └── RemoveClientCommand.cs
│   │   └── Loans
│   │       ├── ListClientLoansCommand.cs
│   │       ├── LoanBookCommand.cs
│   │       └── ReturnBookCommand.cs
│   ├── ICommand.cs
│   └── Menus          
│       └── MainMenu.cs         → Command dispatcher 
│          (dictionary-based)
├── Interfaces
│   ├── IBookRepository.cs
│   ├── IBookService.cs
│   ├── IClientRepository.cs
│   ├── IClientService.cs
│   ├── IFileStorageService.cs
│   ├── ILoanRepository.cs
│   ├── ILoanService.cs
│   └── IRepository.cs
├── LibraryBookTracker.csproj
├── Models
│   ├── BaseEntity.cs
│   ├── Book.cs
│   ├── Client.cs
│   └── Loan.cs
├── Program.cs          → Manual dependency wiring + app entry point 
├── Repositories
│   ├── BookRepository.cs
│   ├── ClientRepository.cs
│   └── LoanRepository.cs
└── Services
    ├── BookService.cs
    ├── ClientService.cs
    ├── FileStorageService.cs
    └── LoanService.cs
```

## Design Decisions & Tradeoffs

### Save to file on every mutation
Data is persisted to JSON after every add, remove, loan, or return operation rather than on a manual save or only on exit.

- **Why:** The app is small and the data set is minimal, so the I/O cost is negligible. The gain is reliability — there is no risk of losing data if the app crashes or the user exits without saving.
- **Tradeoff:** Slightly more disk writes. Acceptable for this scale.

### Loan history is never deleted
When a book is returned, the `Loan` record has its `ReturnDate` set but is kept in the repository. Loans are never removed.

- **Why:** Preserves a full audit trail of all past loans per client. `GetByClient` returns the complete history, and active loans are identified by `ReturnDate == null`.
- **Tradeoff:** The loans file grows over time. For a small library this is not a concern.

### Loan as a separate entity
A dedicated `Loan` entity links `Book` and `Client` by Id instead of embedding loan data directly on the `Book` or `Client` models.

- **Why:** Separation of responsibilities — each entity owns only its own data. It also reduces coupling: `BookService` and `ClientService` don't need to know about each other. Adding new loan-related fields (e.g. due date, fine) only affects the `Loan` model and `LoanService`.
- **Tradeoff:** Requires joining across repositories to display full loan details (e.g. book title alongside a loan record).

## Running

```bash
dotnet run --project LibraryBookTracker
```

title: Finance Tracker (CLI)
description: CLI app to track personal income and expenses built with .NET 9, C#, xUnit and Moq
readme:
# Finance Tracker

A CLI application to track personal income and expenses, built with .NET 9 and C#.

## How to run
```bash
dotnet run --project FinanceTracker
```

## How to test
```bash
dotnet test
```

## Project structure
```
FinanceTracker/
├── Interfaces      # Contracts for services and repositories
│   ├── IFileStorageService.cs
│   ├── ITransactionRepository.cs
│   └── ITransactionService.cs
├── Models           # Domain models and enums
│   ├── Enums
│   │   ├── CategoryType.cs
│   │   └── TransactionType.cs
│   └── Transaction.cs
├── Program.cs       # Entry point and dependency wiring
├── Repositories     # Data access
│   └── TransactionRepository.cs
├── Services         # Business logic
│   ├── FileStorageService.cs
│   └── TransactionService.cs
├── transactions.json #FileStorage
└── UI
    └── ConsoleUI.cs  # Menu loop and user interaction
```

## Architecture decisions

- **`record` for `Transaction`** — transactions are immutable by design; a transaction is never edited, only removed
- **`ITransactionRepository` and `ITransactionService` interfaces** — decouples business logic from data access; allows swapping implementations without changing consumers
- **`FileStorageService` separate from `TransactionRepository`** — persistence is an infrastructure concern, not a domain concern
- **Save on every mutation** — simpler than tracking dirty state; acceptable tradeoff for a CLI app with small datasets
- **`KeyNotFoundException` on invalid remove** — fails loudly instead of silently; easier to debug

## Known tradeoffs

- Data stored in local JSON — in production this would be a database
- No authentication — data is not isolated per user
- No pagination — all transactions are loaded into memory at startup
- No edit/update operation — by design; transactions are immutable

## What I would add next

- Unit tests for `TransactionRepository`
- A monthly summary with top 3 expenses using LINQ
- Dependency injection container instead of manual wiring in `Program.cs`

## Save to File: Automatic vs Manual

Currently, the application calls `SaveToFileAsync` automatically after every change (add/remove). This ensures that data is always persisted immediately, reducing the risk of data loss if the app crashes.

**Trade-offs:**
- **Pros:**
  - Simplicity: No need to track unsaved changes or manage a 'dirty' state.
  - Data safety: Every operation is atomic from the user's perspective; changes are never lost if the app exits unexpectedly.
- **Cons:**
  - Performance: For large datasets or frequent operations, saving after every change can be slow.
  - Flexibility: Harder to implement batch operations or 'undo' functionality, since every change is persisted right away.

## Manual Atomicity Handling

To ensure atomicity in write operations (add/remove), the service uses a try/catch block: all changes are made in memory first, and only then persisted with `SaveToFileAsync`. If an exception occurs during saving, the previous state is restored (manual rollback), reverting any changes made to the in-memory list.

**Advantages:**
- Simulates transactions even without a database
- Prevents inconsistencies if saving fails

**Limitations:**
- Rollback only works while the application is running (does not cover power loss or crashes between operations)

This approach is sufficient for a simple CLI, but in larger systems it's recommended to use real database transactions.

## Thread Safety and Robustness

The repository now uses a `ReaderWriterLockSlim` to guard **all** operations on in-memory and file storage. This means:

- **Full thread safety** for all operations:
  - Multiple threads can safely list/query transactions concurrently.
  - All mutation operations (add, remove, load-from-file, save-to-file) are exclusive and never race.
  - File reads/writes and in-memory mutations are always performed with the appropriate lock.
- **Atomic snapshots:**
  - `SaveToFileAsync` takes a consistent snapshot using a read-lock, blocking parallel mutations while reading but still allowing other snapshot reads.
- **No partial reads/writes:**
  - It's impossible for a load/save to overlap and cause file corruption or stale/incomplete reads, even if two UI sessions trigger them at the same time.

**Design rationale:**
- `ReaderWriterLockSlim` is the correct C# primitive when you want many readers but exclusive writers.
- This pattern means it is now safe to access from many threads, or even from multiple UI tasks (or future API endpoints) with zero risk of data races or corruption.
- All code is async/await friendly—locks only wrap minimal code and never cross thread boundaries.

**Error Handling:**
- File and memory errors are reported with clear, specific exceptions (`IOException`, `KeyNotFoundException`, etc.), ensuring robust detection and diagnosability.

This approach is robust and scalable for small- to medium-sized apps that need safe, immediate persistence with zero risk of concurrency bugs.

### Async File I/O and Snapshots
- Each save/load operation works on a complete snapshot of the transactions in memory, taken under lock for correctness.
- The file write (save) happens asynchronously right after the lock is released, which means:
  - It is *never* possible for the file to be corrupted or partially written, regardless of how often or concurrently save/load/add/remove is called.
  - Very rapid add/remove cycles may result in a saved file that slightly lags the absolute latest state in RAM (the save always reflects a real, past consistent state, matching best practices in .NET async/locking apps).
- This design is safe for real-world multi-session, multi-thread, or even future async API usage without additional concerns.

title: Vanilla HTTP Web Server
description: Simple multithreaded HTTP server in Java, serving static files via raw sockets with clean OOP design.
readme:
# Vanilla Web Server

A simple multithreaded **HTTP web server** built entirely in **Java**, designed to provide a clear understanding of low-level client-server communication and the HTTP protocol.

The server listens for incoming connections and serves static resources from the `src/main/www` directory, using a **fixed thread pool** to handle multiple clients concurrently.


---

## Features
- Handles multiple client connections concurrently using `ExecutorService`
- Parses basic HTTP `GET` requests
- Serves static resources (`.html`, `.css`, `.js`, `.png`, `.ico`)
- Supports **JavaScript ES modules** with correct MIME types
- Automatically determines `Content-Type` via a dedicated `ContentType` enum
- Ignores query strings when resolving filesystem paths
- Returns a custom **404.html** page when resources are not found
- Clean, well-documented codebase with **Javadoc** and clear separation of concerns

---

## How to Run

1. **Compile** the project (e.g., in IntelliJ or using Maven).  
2. **Run** the `Main` class:
   ```bash
   java com.codeforall.online.webserver.Main
   ```
3. Open your browser and visit:  
   👉 [http://localhost:9001](http://localhost:9001)

---

## Example Console Output

```
INFO: Listening at port 9001
INFO: new connection from 127.0.0.1:54328
INFO: Request received: GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
```

---

## Screenshot
![WebServer Running](images/webserver_running.png)

---

## Technologies Used
- Java 17 
- Java Networking (Sockets)
- Concurrency (`ExecutorService`)  
- Java I/O  
- Stream API  
- Logging (`java.util.logging`)

---

## What I Learned

Building this project from scratch gave me a deeper understanding of how web
servers work at a low level, beyond using frameworks.

Through this project, I learned:

- How HTTP requests are structured and how to manually parse request lines
- The importance of separating URL paths from query strings when resolving files
- How browsers depend on correct MIME types, especially for JavaScript ES modules
- How to serve different types of static resources (`HTML`, `CSS`, `JS`, images)
- How to handle multiple client connections using a fixed thread pool
- How to structure a clean and maintainable backend without relying on frameworks
- Why higher-level frameworks abstract many of these concerns and when they become valuable

---

## Author
**Kátia Vilarinho**  
Developed as part of a Java Full-Stack Bootcamp (Code For All_).                          
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/kátia-vilarinho                              
Portfolio: https://katiavilarinho.dev                

---

*"Simple, clean, and built from scratch — a true vanilla web server."*

title: Task Manager (CLI)
description: First standalone Java application I designed from scratch. Handles task management via command line, with full file persistence and a modular class structure. Future versions will adopt MVC and web integration.
readme:
# Task Manager (Console Application)

![Task Manager running](images/task_manager_running.png)

A simple **console-based Task Manager** built in Java.  
It allows adding, listing, completing, and deleting tasks, with automatic file-based persistence.

---

## Features

- **ADD** – Add a new task (incomplete by default)
- **LST** – List all tasks
- **DONE** – Mark a task as completed
- **DEL** – Delete a task by ID
- **HELP** – Show all available commands
- **SAVE** – Manually save tasks to file (optional)
- **EXIT** – Save and exit the application

---

## Storage Format

Tasks are stored in the file **`tasks.dat`** in a simple text-based format:

```
[ ] id: 1 - Buy milk  
[x] id: 2 - Study sockets  
```

- `[ ]` → incomplete
- `[x]` → completed

Each task has a **unique ID**, automatically generated and managed in memory by the repository.  
The file is recreated on each save to ensure consistency between runs.

---

## How to Run

1. **Clone the repository:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Kvilarinho/taskmanager.git
   cd taskmanager
   ```

2. **Build with Maven:**
   ```bash
   mvn clean package
   ```

3. **Run the application:**
   ```bash
   java -jar target/taskmanager-1.1-jar-with-dependencies.jar  
   ```

---

## Example Session

```
Enter a command:
ADD Buy milk
Task added successfully with ID: 1

ADD Study sockets
Task added successfully with ID: 2

LST
[ ] id: 1 - Buy milk
[ ] id: 2 - Study sockets

DONE 1
Task 1 marked as done 

LST
[x] id: 1 - Buy milk
[ ] id: 2 - Study sockets

DEL 2
Task 2 removed successfully

EXIT
Bye!
```

---

## Technical Notes

- Implements the **Strategy Pattern** via a `Map<Command, Function>` for dynamic command execution.
- Tasks are persisted automatically to `tasks.dat` after every change.
- Unique IDs are managed in memory through `TaskRepository#getNextId()`.
- Error handling covers invalid commands, incorrect input, and I/O exceptions.
- Modular architecture with clear separation between:
    - **Commands layer** (`functionalities`)
    - **Persistence layer** (`TaskRepository`)
    - **Controller layer** (`TaskManager`)
    - **Model layer** (`Task`)

---

## Future Improvements (v2)

- Introduce **unit tests** 
- Introduce new commands
- Add filters for completed/uncompleted tasks
- Add timestamps for task creation/completion
- Support editing existing task descriptions
- Transition to a **Java MVC Web version** (Spring Boot + Thymeleaf)

---

## Requirements

- **Java 17+**
- **Maven 3.8+**

---

title: Concurrent TCP Chat
description: Concurrent TCP chat application with multi-client support, command system, private messaging, and admin mode. Built in Java using sockets, concurrency and clean architecture.
readme:
# Concurrent TCP Chat — Server & Client

A concurrent TCP chat application built in Java, featuring a multi-client server, private messaging (whispers), admin mode with server shutdown, and a simple interactive client.
The system demonstrates concurrency, socket programming, command parsing, clean architecture, and unit testing with JUnit + Mockito.

![Server running](/images/tcp_chatserver_running.png)

---

## Overview

This repository contains **two separate Java applications**:

- **ChatServer** — a concurrent TCP server that accepts multiple clients, broadcasts public messages, handles commands, and supports admin-level operations.
- **Client** — a terminal-based TCP client that connects to the server, reads keyboard input, and displays messages in real time.

Both applications run independently and communicate over TCP sockets.

---

## Features

### Server
- Accepts multiple clients concurrently
- Broadcasts messages
- Private messaging (/whisper)
- Admin mode (/admin)
- Server shutdown (/shutdown)
- Thread-safe client management

### Client
- Real-time messaging over TCP
- Graceful exit (/quit)
- Separate threads for input/output

---

## Project Structure

```
Concurrent-TCP-Chat/
├── ChatServer/
├── Client/
├── images/
│   └── tcp_chatserver_running.png
└── README.md
```

---

## Commands

### Client Commands
| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| /help | List commands |
| /list | Show connected users |
| /name <newName> | Change username |
| /whisper <user> <msg> | Private message |
| /admin <password> | Admin login |
| /quit | Leave chat |

### Admin Only
| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| /shutdown | Shut down server |

---

## How to Run

### Start the Server

```
cd ChatServer
mvn clean package
java -jar target/ChatServer-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar
```

### Start a Client

```
cd Client
mvn clean package
java -jar target/Client-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar
```

---

## Unit Tests

Run tests:

```
mvn test
```

Includes tests for:

- Client
- ReaderThread
- KeyboardThread
- ChatServer
- ClientHandler

---

## Javadoc

Generate documentation:

```
mvn javadoc:javadoc
```

Output:

```
target/site/apidocs/
```



---

description: Game of the year - 2D Java game built with OOP, enums, factory pattern, randomization logic, and file I/O for persistent high scores.
readme: # Bullseye Arcade-style 2D **target practice** game built in Java. Move the player vertically and **shoot arrows** to hit the bullseye while avoiding obstacles. Different arrow types have different **speed** and **score** values. Built with OOP (inheritance, enums, factory) and the **SimpleGraphics** library. --- ## 🎮 Gameplay - **Controls:** - `↑ / ↓` – move the player - `Space` – shoot - `S` - start - `Q` - quit game - `R` - return - **Arrow types (randomized):** - **Blue** – very fast, medium score - **Green** – very slow, high score - **Red** – normal speed, base score - **Obstacles:** spawn randomly; **colliding costs −10 points**. - **Goal:** maximize your score by timing shots and managing arrow speed vs. target position. --- ## Features - OOP design with **inheritance** and **composition** - **Enums** for arrow configuration (sprite, speed, score) - **Factory pattern** to create game entities - Keyboard handling via a dedicated `MyKeyboard` class - Simple 2D rendering with **SimpleGraphics** - High-score tracking (`HighScoreManager`) and game state handling (`GameState`) --- ## Project structure ``` . ├─ jar/ # packaged .jar ├─ lib/ # third-party libs (SimpleGraphics) ├─ resources/ # sprites, sounds ├─ src/com/codeforall/online/bullseye/ │ ├─ Main.java │ ├─ game/ │ │ ├─ Arena.java │ │ ├─ Game.java │ │ ├─ GameState.java │ │ ├─ HighScoreManager.java │ │ ├─ MyKeyboard.java │ │ └─ Sfx.java │ ├─ playables/ │ │ ├─ Collidables.java │ │ ├─ Entity.java │ │ ├─ Player.java │ │ ├─ arrows/ │ │ │ ├─ Arrows.java │ │ │ └─ ArrowTypes.java │ │ ├─ obstacle/ │ │ │ ├─ Obstacle.java │ │ │ └─ ObstacleType.java │ │ └─ target/ │ │ ├─ Direction.java │ │ ├─ Target.java │ │ └─ TargetFactory.java ├─ build.xml # Ant build script └─ .gitignore ``` --- ## UML Diagram The initial class design was created using [MermaidChart](https://www.mermaidchart.com/app/projects/58545485-6851-4bad-973c-65e455e56b7d/diagrams/09cd24dd-a293-4801-acb0-4fd7ece9a00a/share/invite/...). It represents the first version of the game's class structure before small implementation adjustments. 📄 [View UML source file](docs/bullseye_uml_initial.mmd) ![Bullseye UML Diagram](docs/Bullseye___Mermaid_Chart-2025-08-22-201240.png) ## Run locally > Requires Java (JDK 17+ recommended) and Ant (optional, if you want to rebuild). ### Option A — Run the prebuilt JAR ``` java -jar jar/bullseye.jar ``` ### Option B — Build & run with Ant ```bash ant clean ant jar java -jar jar/bullseye.jar ``` If you change assets, keep paths consistent with `resources/` and the enum `ArrowTypes`. --- ## Design notes - **ArrowTypes enum** centralizes per-type config (sprite path, speed, score). - **Entities** share common behavior via `Entity` + **Collidables** interface. - **Factory** centralizes creation of playables/obstacles to keep `Game` lean. - **Game loop** updates positions, checks collisions, and renders each frame. - **Keyboard input** is handled by a dedicated `MyKeyboard` class, keeping the game logic separate and cleaner. --- ## Tech stack - **Java** (OOP, enums, inheritance) - **SimpleGraphics** for drawing and input - **Ant** for build/packaging --- ## Future improvements - Difficulty scaling (spawn rates, speeds) - Pause/menu screens and better HUD - Power-ups and arrow inventory - Extra SFX/music and sprite polish --- ## Credits Developed by a team of four colleagues as part of the **Code for All** bootcamp.

title: Team Safety Monitor
description: Team Safety Monitor is a full-stack web application that tracks work patterns and workload metrics to detect early signs of overload and prevent burnout before it happens.
readme:
# Team Safety Monitor ## Overview Team Safety Monitor is a web-based application designed to promote healthier and more sustainable team workloads, improving productivity and long-term efficiency. The application helps prevent overwork by tracking working hours and identifying when individuals or teams are approaching unsafe workload levels. Team members can log their work hours, review their personal work history, and receive alerts when they are nearing predefined safety limits. Team administrators have access to aggregated and anonymized team data, allowing them to monitor overall workload trends and historical work entries at a team level, without visibility into individual identities. This approach ensures organizational transparency while protecting individual privacy and preventing potential misuse of personal workload data.

--- ## Architecture Overview Team Safety Monitor is built as a Single Page Application (SPA) with a clear separation between frontend and backend responsibilities. The frontend is responsible for user interaction, navigation, and data visualization. All navigation is handled client-side using hash-based routing, allowing smooth transitions between views without full page reloads. The backend exposes a RESTful API responsible for business logic, validation, data aggregation, and persistence. This separation ensures scalability, maintainability, and a clean distribution of responsibilities. --- ## Roles and Permissions The system supports two main roles: ### Team Members - Log work hours - View their own workload trends - View their own work history - Receive alerts when approaching unsafe work thresholds ### Team Admins - Monitor overall team workload - Review anonymized historical work entries at a team level - Make workload decisions based on team trends rather than individual tracking --- ## Privacy & Ethics by Design Team Safety Monitor was designed with privacy as a core principle. Team administrators have access only to aggregated and anonymized team workload data. While they can review the team’s historical work entries and workload trends, they cannot identify individual team members or access personal work histories. This design prevents individual surveillance, reduces pressure on team members, and encourages honest reporting of work hours, promoting a healthier and more ethical approach to workload monitoring. --- ## Routing and Application Flow The frontend follows a Single Page Application (SPA) model using hash-based routing. Navigation is handled entirely on the client side, enabling dynamic view rendering without server-side page reloads. This approach was chosen to simplify local development and avoid server-side routing dependencies while keeping the application responsive and lightweight. The backend remains fully decoupled from navigation concerns and focuses exclusively on exposing REST API endpoints and enforcing domain rules. --- ## Technologies ### Frontend Technologies - HTML - CSS - JavaScript (Vanilla JS) - Single Page Application (SPA) - Hash-based routing - REST API consumption ### Backend Technologies - Java - Spring Boot - REST API - PostgreSQL - JPA / Hibernate - Bean Validation --- ## How to Deploy ### Prerequisites Make sure you have the following installed: - Java 17+ - Maven - PostgreSQL - Git - IntelliJ IDEA (recomended) ### Backend Setup 1. Clone the repository: ```bash git clone git@github.com:AlienGamer29/team_safety_monitor.git 2.Open the backend project in InteliJ IDEA: - Open IntelliJ IDEA - Click on "Open" - Choose the backend directory of the cloned repository 2. Create a PostgreSQL database: ```sql CREATE DATABASE team_safety_monitor; ``` 3. Configure the database connection in application.properties: ```properties spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/team_safety_monitor spring.datasource.username=your_username spring.datasource.password=your_password ``` 4. Build and run the backend: ```bash mvn clean install mvn spring-boot:run ``` The backend will be accessible at `http://localhost:8081/teamsafetymonitor`. ### Frontend Setup 1. Open the frontend directory: 2. Open `index.html` in your web browser or serve it using a simple local server (recommended): ```bash npx serve ``` 3. Ensure the frontend is configured to communicate with the backend at `http://localhost:8081/teamsafetymonitor`. ### Database Initialization - The database schema is automatically created on application startup using Hibernate. - This behavior is enabled via the `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=create` configuration. - This setup simplifies local deployment and onboarding for new developers. - For production environments, schema generation should be disabled and managed explicitly. --- ## What We Learned Throughout the development of Team Safety Monitor, we gained several important insights that went beyond technical implementation. One of the most valuable lessons was the importance of planning before writing code. Clearly defining the domain, user roles, and overall application flow early on proved essential to reduce rework and avoid architectural inconsistencies. We also learned how critical it is for all team members to fully understand the complete application flow — from frontend interactions and routing to backend validation and data persistence. Gaps in this shared understanding can quickly lead to fragmented implementations and poorly organized code, particularly on the frontend. This experience highlighted the need for stronger upfront alignment, clearer architectural guidelines, and better communication when working on shared frontend codebases. Finally, the project reinforced the importance of clear communication, shared ownership, and thoughtful separation of concerns when building full-stack applications in a team environment. --- ## Future Features The following features are planned as future improvements to extend the platform’s capabilities and provide deeper insights into team well-being and productivity. ### Authentication and Authorization - User authentication system with secure login - Secure session handling and protected API endpoints ### Extended Work Metrics - Support for additional work entry data, such as: - Overtime hours - Extra shifts or exceptional work periods - End-of-month summaries with aggregated workload statistics - Clear separation between regular work hours and overtime data ### Stress and Well-being Indicators - Introduction of stress-level indicators based on workload patterns - Detection of risk signals related to sustained overwork - Visual indicators to highlight potential burnout risks at team level ### Dashboard and Data Visualization - Interactive dashboards with visual representations of workload data - Charts and graphs showing: - Workload trends over time - Overtime evolution - Stress and risk indicators - Improved data visualization to support informed decision-making ### Frontend Code Organization - Improve frontend code structure and modularization - Implement component-based architecture for better maintainability - Clear separation of concerns between views, services, controllers, state management, routing and utilities ### User Experience Improvements - Improved dashboard layout and visual hierarchy - Enhanced responsiveness for different screen sizes - Clearer visual feedback for alerts and workload thresholds - Smoother navigation between dashboard sections - Improved accessibility and readability of charts and data --- ## Project Management and Collaboration Tools - **Trello** – Task management and project coordination - **Discord** – Team communication and meetings --- ## Contributors -
